graph_contract_v1.relation: Supplies the immutable valid Graph identity, unbounded positive generation domain, and external-gate topology; this contract neither copies nor mutates the Graph. Dependencies within one external join are valid, while an edge leaving any containing manual-gate or corrective-join is GRAPH_INVALID before transition binding.

node_result_v1.relation: The Input schema carries only a Node Result object envelope. After basic Input envelope structural admission and bounded canonical byte admission, the complete proposed Node Result is validated through the existing validate_node_result owner and content-digest bound without defining a second Node Result shape.

runtime_state_contract_v1.relation: Defines the language-neutral snapshot and writer boundary; this contract consumes observed identity labels only.

runtime_state_v1.relation: Supplies graph, run, authority, controller, revision, sequence, node, attempt, and previous-status snapshot identities.

runtime_event_v1.relation: Supplies the last-event sequence correlation boundary. A transition Result is not a Runtime Event.

resolver_admission_semantics.scope: These limits constrain only a pure Transition Resolver invocation. Resolver admission does not change Graph Contract v1 validity, does not narrow any Graph identity or array domain, does not require another host or runtime to reject the Graph, and grants no execution authority.
resolver_admission_semantics.graph_contract_non_narrowing: A Graph above a Transition Resolver admission limit may still be valid under Graph Contract v1 and is not automatically an invalid Graph. Resolver admission failure does not shrink, replace, or modify the Graph Contract.
resolver_admission_semantics.ready_alignment: The numeric Graph admission limits intentionally equal the existing Ready Resolver limits, but the Transition Resolver and Ready Resolver execute their contracts independently. Transition resolution does not call the Ready Resolver and does not reuse a Ready Resolver admission decision.
resolver_admission_semantics.graph_measurement: First measure the complete supplied Graph as canonical strict JSON bytes using canonical_digests.canonical_json. Use a bounded counter that stops as soon as byte 8388609 would be emitted; an implementation need not materialize or retain an unbounded canonical byte string. Exactly 8388608 bytes is admitted. More than 8388608 bytes returns GRAPH_TOO_LARGE before structural or semantic Graph validation.
resolver_admission_semantics.boundary_rule: Every numeric admission bound is inclusive. A value exactly at its bound is admitted; boundary plus one is rejected before Graph validation or transition resolution.
resolver_admission_semantics.structural_preflight: After byte admission, perform only a cheap structural cardinality preflight over top-level nodes and joins and each directly contained node depends_on and resources array and join requires array. Stop counting a collection at its bound plus one. Missing, mistyped, or otherwise malformed structures are not repaired or classified by this preflight and remain for validate_graph_contract after admission.
resolver_admission_semantics.pre_admission_resource_rule: Before byte and structural admission succeed, do not run unbounded cycle traversal, dependency traversal, join resolution, referential-integrity traversal, or construct an unbounded issue collection. Admission failure returns one bounded Error classification without collecting every downstream defect.
resolver_admission_semantics.graph_bytes_overflow: Canonical Graph bytes greater than max_graph_canonical_bytes return only GRAPH_TOO_LARGE Error and no Result or partial transition.
resolver_admission_semantics.structural_overflow: Any nodes, joins, per-node depends_on, per-node resources, or per-join requires cardinality greater than its corresponding Transition Resolver bound returns only RESOLUTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED before validate_graph_contract. This admission classification is not GRAPH_INVALID; Graph Contract validity has not been narrowed or decided by the preflight.
resolver_admission_semantics.no_partial_processing: The Transition Resolver never rewrites, truncates, splits, samples, or partially processes a Graph to cross an admission limit and never disguises an admission overflow as Graph invalid.
resolver_admission_semantics.classification_boundary: The ordered Graph outcomes are mutually exclusive: byte overflow is GRAPH_TOO_LARGE; admitted bytes with structural overflow is RESOLUTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; fully admitted Graph Contract failure is GRAPH_INVALID; fully admitted valid Graph with graph ID, generation, or digest mismatch is GRAPH_BINDING_MISMATCH.

snapshot_binding.input_meaning: Input is an observed snapshot only. Contract validation does not prove that the snapshot is still current.
snapshot_binding.node_result_binding: The complete Node Result is bound by node_result_digest; its node_id must equal the input node_id and the exact proposed status must become next_status only when the existing transition owner allows the pair.
snapshot_binding.stale_result_rule: A Result is non-reusable if any binding, attempt identity, revision, sequence, authority/controller identity, input digest, or Node Result digest no longer matches.

graph_validation.argument: The pure resolver receives the complete supplied Graph separately from Transition Resolution Input and treats it as immutable.
graph_validation.canonical_byte_admission: First perform resolver_admission_semantics.graph_measurement and return only GRAPH_TOO_LARGE if the bounded canonical byte counter exceeds max_graph_canonical_bytes.
graph_validation.structural_cardinality_preflight: Second perform resolver_admission_semantics.structural_preflight and return only RESOLUTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED if any resolver cardinality bound is exceeded.
graph_validation.validator_rule: After both admission checks succeed, validate the admitted Graph through the existing Stage 2B validate_graph_contract owner. Its successful result supplies semantic_digest. Graph-aware Node Result validation may invoke that same owner once more through validate_node_result; the success path performs no other Graph validation and caches no unvalidated input.
graph_validation.invalid_outcome: If validate_graph_contract reports that the Graph is invalid, return only GRAPH_INVALID Error. Never classify an invalid Graph as GRAPH_BINDING_MISMATCH, calculate a digest for it, emit Result, or emit a partial transition.
graph_validation.digest_rule: The single successful Stage 2B owner validation supplies the existing canonical Graph semantic digest. The resolver does not invoke Graph validation again on the admitted snapshot.

graph_binding.precondition: Graph Contract v1 validation has succeeded and the existing canonical Graph digest has been calculated.

comparisons.graph_id: Input graph_id equals the validated Graph graph_id.
comparisons.graph_generation: Input graph_generation equals the validated Graph generation.
comparisons.graph_digest: Input graph_digest equals the existing canonical Graph digest.

graph_binding.mismatch_outcome: Only a valid Graph whose graph ID, generation, or digest does not match Transition Resolution Input yields GRAPH_BINDING_MISMATCH Error and no Result.

semantic_validation.generation_domain: Graph generation uses the unbounded positive mathematical JSON integer domain from Graph Contract v1. JSON booleans are invalid; finite mathematically integral representations such as 1 and 1.0 compare and canonicalize identically; non-integral and non-finite values are invalid. Canonical encoding supports arbitrarily large admitted integers without changing Python or host process-global digit limits.

transition_input.structure_rule: After Graph admission and validation succeed, perform bounded strict-JSON admission of the complete Transition Resolution Input before field inspection, sorting, formatting, or any user-defined dunder can run. Then perform basic structural admission through input.schema.json before Graph binding. The Input schema remains an envelope validator and does not validate complete Node Result v1 semantics, authority-change status, decision semantics, graph-aware node/proposal references, read-only changed paths, node binding, or transition legality.
transition_input.invalid_outcome: A missing, mistyped, malformed, or otherwise structurally invalid Input envelope returns only REQUIRED_INPUT_INVALID Error and does not reach canonical byte counting, Node Result, binding, authority-change, or transition classification.
transition_input.canonical_byte_admission: Before inspecting Input fields, measure and validate the complete Transition Resolution Input as canonical strict JSON using canonical_digests.canonical_json. Use a bounded counter that stops as soon as byte 16777217 would be emitted. Exactly 16777216 bytes is admitted.
transition_input.too_large_outcome: A structurally admitted Input envelope whose canonical byte count exceeds 16777216 returns only INPUT_TOO_LARGE Error before graph-aware validate_node_result, node binding, authority-change status classification, transition legality, or digest calculation.

semantic_validation.graph_classification_boundary: GRAPH_TOO_LARGE applies only when the bounded canonical Graph byte calculation exceeds 8388608. RESOLUTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED applies only after byte admission when a Transition Resolver structural cardinality exceeds its bound, is not GRAPH_INVALID, and does not decide Graph Contract validity. An admitted invalid Graph yields only GRAPH_INVALID and never GRAPH_BINDING_MISMATCH. After one successful Graph owner validation supplies its semantic digest, Input processing proceeds in this order: bounded strict-JSON admission before any field formatting or dunder invocation, basic envelope structural admission, Graph binding, graph-aware Node Result validation, node binding, authority-change status classification, transition legality, then digests.

node_binding.precondition: Evaluate only after Graph admission, validation, and binding, basic Input envelope structural admission, bounded canonical byte admission, and graph-aware validate_node_result have succeeded.

node_result.validation_rule: After basic Transition Resolution Input envelope structural admission and bounded canonical byte admission succeed, validate the complete Node Result through its existing graph-aware owner before node binding, authority-change status, or transition legality classification. Do not copy or redefine Node Result v1 validation in the Input schema.
node_result.graph_aware_scope: validate_node_result owns complete Node Result semantics for missing required Node Result fields, invalid status, missing or invalid authority decision, unknown graph node, unknown proposed_next_nodes targets, read-only node changed_paths, bounded findings, no-action evidence, and all other Node Result v1 structural and semantic failures.
node_result.invalid_outcome: A supplied Node Result object that fails existing graph-aware validate_node_result returns only NODE_RESULT_INVALID Error and never NODE_BINDING_MISMATCH, AUTHORITY_CHANGE_STATUS_INVALID, TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED, or Result.

authority_change_status.precondition: Evaluate only after Graph admission, validation, and binding, basic Input envelope structural admission, bounded canonical byte admission, graph-aware validate_node_result, and node binding have succeeded. Missing or invalid authority decision remains NODE_RESULT_INVALID because it is owned by valid Node Result validation.
authority_change_status.required_decision: existing Node Result v1 non-empty bounded decision
authority_change_status.classification_rule: For an otherwise valid Node Result with authority_change true, any non-HANDOFF status returns AUTHORITY_CHANGE_STATUS_INVALID before transition legality is evaluated. Missing, empty, too-long, or otherwise invalid decision remains NODE_RESULT_INVALID, not AUTHORITY_CHANGE_STATUS_INVALID.

semantic_validation.status_projection: For ordinary input, next_status equals node_result.status exactly. For authority change, both node_result.status and next_status are HANDOFF. No status is trimmed, mapped, promoted, or synthesized.
semantic_validation.validation_failure: Any structural Input or Graph, size, binding, Node Result, transition, or authority-change failure yields only Error. Invalid, oversized, or Graph-invalid input has no Result, no partial transition, and no fabricated HANDOFF or BLOCKED substitute.

transition_legality.rule: After Graph admission/validation/binding, basic Input envelope structural admission, bounded canonical byte admission, graph-aware Node Result validation, node binding, and authority-change status validation have succeeded, the pair previous_status and the exact Node Result status must be allowed by the existing owner. This contract's Result schema mirrors that table only as a success-envelope constraint and does not create a different state machine.
transition_legality.terminal_rule: A terminal previous status cannot produce Result.
transition_legality.distinct_outcomes: NO_ACTION_REQUIRED and DONE_WITH_CONCERNS remain their exact proposed statuses and are never mapped to SUCCEEDED.

authority_change.false_green_rule: authority_change true with SUCCEEDED, NO_ACTION_REQUIRED, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, or any non-HANDOFF status is invalid and yields AUTHORITY_CHANGE_STATUS_INVALID Error, never Result.
authority_change.permission_boundary: An authority request does not modify permission, a gate, the Graph, project authority, or runtime authority.

canonical_digests.purpose: Canonical content identity for Stage 4C1 transition decisions. It is not a Stage 5 semantic evidence fingerprint.

node_result_digest.construction: SHA-256(UTF-8 domain separator bytes followed by canonical JSON bytes of the complete valid Node Result v1 instance).

transition_input_digest.construction: SHA-256(UTF-8 domain separator bytes followed by canonical JSON bytes of the complete valid Transition Resolution Input v1 instance).

canonical_digests.validation_order: Resolver-wide Graph admission and the single Graph owner validation follow semantic_validation.deterministic_order. For Transition Resolution Input, first perform bounded strict-JSON admission, rejecting non-string object names without formatting them, duplicate scalar-equivalent names, non-JSON numbers, and invalid Unicode scalar sequences; then validate input.schema.json and Graph binding; then run graph-aware Node Result validation, node binding, authority-change status validation, and transition legality; only then calculate input and Node Result digests. No input or Node Result digest exists for invalid or oversized input.

canonical_json.object_keys: Recursively sort object keys lexicographically by Unicode scalar value sequence.
canonical_json.arrays: Preserve every array in its original order.
canonical_json.separators: Use comma and colon with no insignificant whitespace.
canonical_json.numbers: Only mathematical JSON integer values are admitted by these schemas, following JSON Schema 2020-12 integer semantics. Lexically distinct but mathematically equal forms such as 1, 1.0, and 1e0 canonicalize identically to the shortest base-10 integer 1; negative zero canonicalizes to 0. Encode with no leading plus, leading zero, decimal point, or exponent. JSON booleans are not integers. Reject non-integral numbers, NaN, positive Infinity, and negative Infinity before a digest exists.
canonical_json.string_escaping: Escape quotation mark and reverse solidus. Use the fixed short escapes for backspace, tab, line feed, form feed, and carriage return; encode remaining U+0000 through U+001F controls as lowercase \u00xx. Encode every other Unicode scalar directly as UTF-8, including non-BMP scalars.
canonical_json.surrogates: A valid paired UTF-16 JSON escape denotes its single non-BMP Unicode scalar and canonicalizes to that scalar's direct UTF-8 bytes. Reject every unpaired escape and every lone surrogate code point.
canonical_json.opaque_strings: Preserve the original Unicode scalar sequence and its UTF-8 bytes; never trim, normalize, case-fold, parse as a filesystem path, or otherwise rewrite it.

canonical_digests.opaque_string_rule: Opaque strings undergo no trim, case-fold, path normalization, or Unicode normalization; slash, leading punctuation, non-BMP scalars, and long identities are preserved exactly within the aggregate limit.

node_result.decision: Request authority without mutating the graph.

output_contract.result_meaning: A complete pure success decision for one exact snapshot and Node Result only.
output_contract.error_meaning: A complete bounded failure only, containing no success fields or partial Result.
output_contract.oversized_result: Return RESULT_TOO_LARGE Error; never truncate or emit a partial Result.

race_and_apply_boundary.resolver_scope: The implemented pure resolver may decide only the supplied snapshot and performs no compare-and-swap or current-state proof.
race_and_apply_boundary.required_before_apply: Revalidate graph identity, generation and digest; run, authority and controller identity; node and attempt identity; state revision; last event sequence; input digest; and Node Result digest against the current authorized state.
race_and_apply_boundary.apply_effect: Contract presence and Result presence perform no apply. Only an independently authorized host/runtime writer may map an unchanged decision to later runtime behavior.

semantic_boundaries.runtime_mutation: Contract presence does not create, and a transition decision does not create, an event, state, write, lock, lease, scheduler, agent, execution packet, or runtime-store mutation.
semantic_boundaries.graph_mutation: proposed_next_nodes is digest-bound proposal content only; it does not activate, create, execute, or schedule a node and grants no Graph mutation. Graph evolution remains deferred to Stage 6.
semantic_boundaries.authority: Result is a pure decision and grants no execution, write, gate, Graph-mutation, project-authority, controller, or writer authority. An authority request changes no permission or gate.
semantic_boundaries.ready_resolver: This contract does not call the Ready Resolver and creates no readiness, resource-acquisition, join, scheduling, or agent behavior.
semantic_boundaries.privacy: Input, Result, and Error exclude private reasoning, prompt or transcript content, stdout, stderr, secret or credential material, environment dump content, arbitrary payloads, complete project history, and runtime handles. Error messages remain bounded observable text.

deferred.stage_5: Semantic evidence fingerprinting is not part of these canonical content digests.
deferred.stage_6: Graph evolution and proposal application remain outside this contract.

compatibility: Transition Resolution Contract v1 consumes the Graph Contract v1 external-gate topology before snapshot binding. Dependencies among members of one external join are valid; an edge leaving any containing manual-gate or corrective-join is GRAPH_INVALID and produces no partial Result. Existing Stage 4D Graph semantic digest vectors, Transition Input/Result/Error, Node Result, Runtime State/Event, snapshot binding, authority-change, and content-digest authority boundaries remain unchanged. Resolver and resource presence remain inert and activate no execution. This relation adds no join-to-node edge, WAITING_GATE, SKIPPED, or UNREACHABLE status, scheduler, dynamic Graph rewrite, runtime mutation, permission, gate decision, CLI, or authority grant.

source_authority.reference: Rebuild Stage 4C1 — Transition Resolution Contract v1

packaged_mirror.expectation: This package-resource directory is the canonical owner of all Transition Resolution Contract v1 resources; distributed copies must remain byte-identical.
